In a cohort of 224 adults with chronic Chagasic cardiomyopathy treated with benznidazole, the main predictors for definite treatment interruption or development of severe adverse drug reaction were dose of benznidazol ≥ 6 mg/Kg/day, severity of adverse drug reaction and presence of eosinophilia.

The risk of treatment interruption or severe adverse drug reactions to benznidazol in adults was significantly associated with higher doses of the drug, female sex, presence of eosinophilia and the development of severe adverse reactions.
